html:
The Yerevan Brandy Company is a distillery in Yerevan founded in 1887 by the merchant Nerses Tairyan, whose Ararat brandy became Armenia's best known export.

In 1899 it was bought by the Russian vodka maker Nikolai Shustov, whose brandy won a gold medal in Paris in 1900 and was allowed to be called cognac, an unusual honour outside France. In Soviet times Armenian brandy was a prestige drink across the Soviet Union. The French group Pernod Ricard bought the company in 1998. Brandy, wine and apricots remain among the main farm based exports of Armenia, with grapes grown in the Ararat plain below Mount Ararat.
